Update 2026-11-05: three commits added for the checkpoint's image part, which did not load before. c39294460 "[Bugfix][GLM-5.3] Build the vision tower with the checkpoint's quantization": Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration built the tower without a quant config, after the zai-org FP8 checkpoint that ships it in BF16; GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local quantizes it (MXFP8 attention, W4A16 NVFP4 MLPs and merger, 124 layers listed in quantized_layers), so loading failed on the packed NVFP4 weights (checkpoint [1024, 2048] against parameter [1024, 4096]). The tower now takes declared_quant_config like the attention projections, and the fused attention projection is named qkv as in the checkpoint. 3315505d2 "[Perf][GLM-5.3] Bound the vision tower's activation memory": the tower ran its token-wise steps over all patches at once, 1338 MiB of MLP and merger intermediates for a maximum-size image (31,684 patches); the V2 encoder profiling reserves that on stage 0, and at 524,288 tokens of context the entry then failed to boot with images enabled (1.37 GiB of KV memory left on stage 0, 1.59 GiB needed). Projections, q/k norm, rotary, MLPs and merger now run over 4096 rows at a time, only the attention sees the whole sequence; the dummy image peaks at 720 MiB on a Quadro RTX 8000, in 3.6 s as before. 75fd75d70 adds tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_row_chunks.py (merger and attention projections with and without rotary, chunks of three rows against one piece; a chunking that drops or rescales a chunk fails all three cases).

Under pipeline parallelism with Model Runner V2 the image part also needs #1365 (encoder towers only on the first stage, encoder profiling, bounded dummy video frame search); with #1362 the later stages no longer read the tower either. On our fork all of these run together in our GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local production entry since 2026-11-05 (PP5 over 3x V100 + 2x RTX 8000, --max-model-len 524288, --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":12,"video":0}').

Checks of the quantized tower on a Quadro RTX 8000, against an fp32 tower on exactly dequantized weights: every linear and the ViT attention within 2e-4 to 5e-4 relative L2 (fp16 activations), no NaN or Inf, largest activation 226 (0.3 % of the fp16 range); the embeddings of three photos at 6.12, 3.03 and 5.43 % relative L2 with the row chunks against 6.11, 3.03 and 5.38 % in one piece. A/B/A/B of the entry with images against the same entry before (without these commits, #1365 and the second commit of #1362, image limit 0), two counted boots each: prefill of 8,687 tokens 4.27 / 4.27 s against 4.29 / 4.17 s, short decode 41.81 / 41.81 tok/s against 41.82 / 41.81 tok/s, GSM8K-30 29 / 29 against 29 / 29, the eight quality answers identical token for token, peak memory of the RTX 8000 on stage 0 +174 MiB, KV of stage 0 2.35 -> 1.85 GiB (pool 676,645 -> 578,061 tokens, still above 524,288). Control run of the installed entry: seven image requests (one or two images, 3,026 to 7,295 prompt tokens, reasoning effort max, at most 4,000 tokens), first token after 2.9 to 6.4 s; six answers describe or transcribe their image correctly (read by hand), the printed medication plan spent all 4,000 tokens on reasoning.

## Purpose

Serve NVIDIA's GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local checkpoint (ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION: NVFP4 routed experts with csf_32x2_v1 compressed block scales, MXFP8 KDA and dense projections, block-FP8 MLA projections) on SM70 and SM75 without converting the checkpoint. Unpacked to E4M3 the expert scales add 8.1 GiB and the model no longer fits five 32/48 GiB cards, so the scales stay compressed on the GPU, and the 8-bit projections stay 8-bit in QPN8 instead of being widened to fp16 at load. Our deployment: PP=5 over three Tesla V100 and two Quadro RTX 8000 with DFlash2, 524,288 tokens of context (docs/design/sm70_glm53_pp5_dflash2_mixed.md, added here).

Stacked PR. The branch sits on #1282 (Triton routes, itself on #1280, #1279, #1278 and #1216; #1222 and #1227 below them are merged). #1274 and #1275, which the boot needs, are merged as well. Above #1282 come three commits that #1274 and #1275 do not carry because #1260 changes the same places (see the duplicate paragraph): a full-precision LM head left to its embedding method with ModelOpt (c05d939cc), no up-projected context reserved for sparse MLA in the profile run (32f394462) and its test (535f60173). Then the GLM commits. Please review from c05d939cc on (git log c05d939cc~1..814c88909).

Groups of the GLM commits:

1. Loading and correctness (d6c8b9e0d, d225cc318, 43567bd4e, 64277a325, a6c286da2): csf_32x2_v1 decoder (with an encoder whose output matches the reference implementation in TensorFold byte for byte) and an expander that fills a shared QPN scale raster with the routed experts before each grouped skinny call (fixed launch shape, CUDA-graph safe; experts opt in through the CsfScaleConsumer protocol, other experts are rejected when the method is built); ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION detection of weight_scale_encoding and a CSF loader for the expert scales; FP8_PB_WO linears through w8a8_block_fp8_linear (in modelopt.py, so for every architecture); block scales held next to their weights across AutoWeightsLoader calls (before, a scale that preceded its FP8 weight in the shards was silently dropped, the MLA projections stayed zero and the output was garbled); csf32 parts routed by their checkpoint name; the indexer query built in fp16 on Turing like the indexer op; Turing admitted on the FP16 sparse-MLA, KPool, indexer, mHC and KDA paths, each gate reading the capability of the worker's own device. Three GLM/ModelOpt test files that failed on main as well follow the current code.
2. Sparse MLA prefill with FP8 KV on cuBLAS blocks (e9e65989c): the Triton kernel (tl.dot as FMA before SM80, 78-87 % of the prefill compute) is replaced by the decode's gather/dequantize + cuBLAS GEMM route in blocks of 16 tokens. In an nsys profile of a 14,038-token prefill this part took 68.72 s before and 10.75 s after.
3. 8-bit projections in QPN8 (451b7c54a, 7a3bc12fb, 687de2508, 43db66d52): a third QPN8 scale mode [K/32, N] for MXFP8 (prepare, dequantization bit-identical to load-time unpacking, GEMV for M <= 8; accepts E8M0 exponents 95..134, which are exact in fp16); MXFP8 KDA q/k/v, KDA o_proj and the dense MLPs kept as MXFP8 linears (the KDA layer keeps its quant config and splits in_proj into a quantized qkv and a BF16 b/f_a/g_a part; all KDA layers of a pipeline stage must agree, a mixed checkpoint stops at load with an error); a Turing m16n8k8 path for the row-group scales at M 9..512; MLA q_b_proj, kv_b_proj and o_proj kept as block FP8 when the checkpoint names them. The MXFP8 kernel choice now sees the layer's shape (693efc243): Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig carries the partition's (N, K), the ModelOpt, online and compressed-tensors MXFP8 methods choose their kernel in create_weights, and the QPN8 kernel declines shapes it cannot pack (N % 32, K % 16, no split-K for K), so such a layer keeps Marlin (SM75) or the emulation (SM70) as before. This kernel comes first for every MXFP8 linear on SM70/SM75, not only for this checkpoint.
4. CSF expansion speed (4604639ef, cbab57d28, 3a6639a27, a5d6e0e4b, b80ac11fc): grid bounded by the expert count (same bound as the skinny MoE grid), more programs for decode, a CUDA kernel (plain CUDA, four raster positions per thread, exception records written in the same pass) called through a _custom_ops wrapper.
5. Five-bit scale planes (de0f449a7, 6d39be98c, 3282e0d1b, c6ca88f15): at load the csf scales are re-encoded as base + 4-bit nibble + 1 high bit per scale in the raster's positions (one block in six has a csf exception record, which a kernel cannot look up in its loop, but the scales of a row span at most 31 in all but the last layers). Decode and prefill read the planes in place; on a stage whose projections are all packed the shared raster is freed. Projections whose rows span more than five bits (layers 36 and 40-44) keep their csf planes and the raster expansion.
6. Memory and deployment (d59fd9814, 76e60ba73, 62248bce9): skinny MoE routing groups built by one Triton program up to 128 slots (19 small torch kernels before; the torch version stays the reference) — this applies to every skinny MoE model; the embedding table can live in pinned host memory through the existing UVA offloader, only when --cpu-offload-params names embed_tokens (--cpu-offload-gb alone keeps its budget for the layers), which frees 1.18 GiB on the first stage and on the DFlash replica of the last stage for the KV pool; the PP5 + DFlash2 layout document.
7. Two commits close the series: the per-shape MXFP8 kernel choice above (693efc243), and a clang-format pass (814c88909) over the native lines of this series (whitespace, comment wrapping and macro line continuations only).

The tower now takes declared_quant_config like the attention projections, and the fused attention projection is named qkv as in the checkpoint. 3315505d2 "[Perf][GLM-5.3] Bound the vision tower's activation memory": the tower ran its token-wise steps over all patches at once, 1338 MiB of MLP and merger intermediates for a maximum-size image (31,684 patches); the V2 encoder profiling reserves that on stage 0, and at 524,288 tokens of context the entry then failed to boot with images enabled (1.37 GiB of KV memory left on stage 0, 1.59 GiB needed). Projections, q/k norm, rotary, MLPs and merger now run over 4096 rows at a time, only the attention sees the whole sequence; the dummy image peaks at 720 MiB on a Quadro RTX 8000, in 3.6 s as before. 75fd75d70 adds tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_row_chunks.py (merger and attention projections with and without rotary, chunks of three rows against one piece; a chunking that drops or rescales a chunk fails all three cases).

Under pipeline parallelism with Model Runner V2 the image part also needs #1365 (encoder towers only on the first stage, encoder profiling, bounded dummy video frame search); with #1362 the later stages no longer read the tower either. On our fork all of these run together in our GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local production entry since 2026-11-05 (PP5 over 3x V100 + 2x RTX 8000, --max-model-len 524288, --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":12,"video":0}').

## Purpose

Serve NVIDIA's GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local checkpoint (ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION: NVFP4 routed experts with csf_32x2_v1 compressed block scales, MXFP8 KDA and dense projections, block-FP8 MLA projections) on SM70 and SM75 without converting the checkpoint. Unpacked to E4M3 the expert scales add 8.1 GiB and the model no longer fits five 32/48 GiB cards, so the scales stay compressed on the GPU, and the 8-bit projections stay 8-bit in QPN8 instead of being widened to fp16 at load. Our deployment: PP=5 over three Tesla V100 and two Quadro RTX 8000 with DFlash2, 524,288 tokens of context (docs/design/sm70_glm53_pp5_dflash2_mixed.md, added here).

Loading and correctness (d6c8b9e0d, d225cc318, 43567bd4e, 64277a325, a6c286da2): csf_32x2_v1 decoder (with an encoder whose output matches the reference implementation in TensorFold byte for byte) and an expander that fills a shared QPN scale raster with the routed experts before each grouped skinny call (fixed launch shape, CUDA-graph safe; experts opt in through the CsfScaleConsumer protocol, other experts are rejected when the method is built); ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION detection of weight_scale_encoding and a CSF loader for the expert scales; FP8_PB_WO linears through w8a8_block_fp8_linear (in modelopt.py, so for every architecture); block scales held next to their weights across AutoWeightsLoader calls (before, a scale that preceded its FP8 weight in the shards was silently dropped, the MLA projections stayed zero and the output was garbled); csf32 parts routed by their checkpoint name; the indexer query built in fp16 on Turing like the indexer op; Turing admitted on the FP16 sparse-MLA, KPool, indexer, mHC and KDA paths, each gate reading the capability of the worker's own device. Three GLM/ModelOpt test files that failed on main as well follow the current code.
2. Sparse MLA prefill with FP8 KV on cuBLAS blocks (e9e65989c): the Triton kernel (tl.dot as FMA before SM80, 78-87 % of the prefill compute) is replaced by the decode's gather/dequantize + cuBLAS GEMM route in blocks of 16 tokens. In an nsys profile of a 14,038-token prefill this part took 68.72 s before and 10.75 s after.
3. 8-bit projections in QPN8 (451b7c54a, 7a3bc12fb, 687de2508, 43db66d52): a third QPN8 scale mode [K/32, N] for MXFP8 (prepare, dequantization bit-identical to load-time unpacking, GEMV for M <= 8; accepts E8M0 exponents 95..134, which are exact in fp16); MXFP8 KDA q/k/v, KDA o_proj and the dense MLPs kept as MXFP8 linears (the KDA layer keeps its quant config and splits in_proj into a quantized qkv and a BF16 b/f_a/g_a part; all KDA layers of a pipeline stage must agree, a mixed checkpoint stops at load with an error); a Turing m16n8k8 path for the row-group scales at M 9..512; MLA q_b_proj, kv_b_proj and o_proj kept as block FP8 when the checkpoint names them. The MXFP8 kernel choice now sees the layer's shape (693efc243): Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig carries the partition's (N, K), the ModelOpt, online and compressed-tensors MXFP8 methods choose their kernel in create_weights, and the QPN8 kernel declines shapes it cannot pack (N % 32, K % 16, no split-K for K), so such a layer keeps Marlin (SM75) or the emulation (SM70) as before. This kernel comes first for every MXFP8 linear on SM70/SM75, not only for this checkpoint.
4. CSF expansion speed (4604639ef, cbab57d28, 3a6639a27, a5d6e0e4b, b80ac11fc): grid bounded by the expert count (same bound as the skinny MoE grid), more programs for decode, a CUDA kernel (plain CUDA, four raster positions per thread, exception records written in the same pass) called through a _custom_ops wrapper.
5. Five-bit scale planes (de0f449a7, 6d39be98c, 3282e0d1b, c6ca88f15): at load the csf scales are re-encoded as base + 4-bit nibble + 1 high bit per scale in the raster's positions (one block in six has a csf exception record, which a kernel cannot look up in its loop, but the scales of a row span at most 31 in all but the last layers). Decode and prefill read the planes in place; on a stage whose projections are all packed the shared raster is freed. Projections whose rows span more than five bits (layers 36 and 40-44) keep their csf planes and the raster expansion.
6. Memory and deployment (d59fd9814, 76e60ba73, 62248bce9): skinny MoE routing groups built by one Triton program up to 128 slots (19 small torch kernels before; the torch version stays the reference) — this applies to every skinny MoE model; the embedding table can live in pinned host memory through the existing UVA offloader, only when --cpu-offload-params names embed_tokens (--cpu-offload-gb alone keeps its budget for the layers), which frees 1.18 GiB on the first stage and on the DFlash replica of the last stage for the KV pool; the PP5 + DFlash2 layout document.
